subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as a first-run onboarding/auth method, and what consent, scope, callback, token-storage, refresh, billing-detection, and fallback contract is acceptable?
rationale: Current code has enough OAuth plumbing to make the feature plausible, but presenting it as one-click onboarding crosses product UX, provider policy, and credential-security boundaries that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve Additive Provider OAuth
options.body: Expose Anthropic OAuth as an additional provider-owned auth method after security, docs, live proof, and fallback requirements are explicit.

options.title: Keep Explicit Auth Paths
options.body: Keep API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI as the supported Anthropic paths and improve wording/docs instead of adding browser OAuth now.

options.title: Prototype Behind Experiment
options.body: Allow an experimental maintainer-owned OAuth path that does not replace current Anthropic setup choices until policy and live proof are strong.

recommendation.title: Approve Additive Provider OAuth
recommendation.body: Expose Anthropic OAuth as an additional provider-owned auth method after security, docs, live proof, and fallback requirements are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on Anthropic auth/setup choices and adjacent provider documentation.
